- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a downward bias correction of 1–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 85% of recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 85% of 30-day moving average for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– values), model tends to overfit short-term noise — apply smoothing filter: average last 3 sentiment values before adjusting forecast.
